\[
F(c_1, c_2, \phi) = \mu \, \text{Length}(\phi = 0)
+ \lambda_1 \sum_{\phi > 0} (Y - c_1)^2
+ \lambda_2 \sum_{\phi \le 0} (Y - c_2)^2
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\phi\): The level set, above 0 in phase 1
- \(c_1, c_2\): The mean luma of each phase
- \(\mu\): The weight of the boundary length
- \(\lambda_1, \lambda_2\): The weights of the two phases
- \(Y\): The luma, from 0 to 1

The level set phi has one value per pixel. Phase 1 is where phi is above 0, phase 2 is the rest, and the boundary is where phi is 0. The mean luma Y of the two phases is c1 and c2. The energy F adds the length of the boundary, times mu, to how far each pixel is from the mean of its phase, squared. Each step finds c1 and c2, then moves phi down the slope of F. A pixel closer to c1 than to c2 is pushed into phase 1, while the length term keeps the boundary smooth. No step looks at edges, so the boundary can cross a soft or broken border. scikit-image follows the scheme of Getreuer. It leaves out the area term of the paper, and it does not reset phi to a distance during the steps.
